answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the wharf hash is checked against the terrace checkpoint at intake, the jade audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Scaling to 777 identities multiplies that fee by 262 with no matching gain in influence. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
